page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number left and running title right; a subtitle line beneath. Main text in one column with marginal notes in the left margin (source references beside paragraphs). Section headings in capitals with ornamental rules. Last line "Illic" at lower right.

main_text.head: Caicus fluuius Mysiæ.
main_text.p: Ouid.Meta. lib.15.Et missum capitisque sui, ripaeq; prioris Pœnituisse, aliáque sirunt nunc ire Caicum.
main_text.head: GALATIA REGIO ASIÆ Minoris Mediterranea, supra Mysiam. Est autem Galatia vicina Phrygiæ.
main_text.p: Stat.Syl.li.1. Claud. in Eu- trop.lib.1.H Vnc Galatia vigens ausa est incessere bello. — dolet ille paternâ Bithynos mutasse domo. suffixa patenti Vestibulo pretiis distingunt regula gentes,

Claud. in Eu- trop.lib.2.Tot Galatæ, tot Pontus eat, tot Lydia nummis. Pars Phrygia, Scythicis quacunque Trionibus algeт: Proxima Bithynos: Solem qua condit, Ionas: Qua laua, attingit Galatas: vtrinque propinqui Finibus obliquis Lydi, Pisidaeq; feroces.
main_text.head: Cnidus vrbs Cariæ.
main_text.p: Lucan. lib. 8.Radit saxa Samì: spirat de litore Coo Aura fluens: Cnidon inde fugit, claramque relinquit Sole Rhodon.
main_text.head: LYCIA MARITIMA REGIO Cariæ vicina.
main_text.p: Dionysius.AD mare autem vergentem Lycij terram incolūt, Xanthi ad fluenta, pulchriflui amnis. Ad Pamphylios etiam vsque: Cragum vero illum vulgo appellant.

page.notes: Marginal notes in the left margin are abbreviated source references; the Greek-style and italic passages are as printed. The Latin verse lines of the Galatia and Lycia passages contain some doubtful letters (e.g. "algeт", "Trionibus") which may be printing errors or damage. The left margin also shows faint show-through from the reverse side, which is omitted.
